A unit test to test the basic functions of {@link BoundedIterator}.

{@link BoundedIterator} decorates another iterator so that only the elements in the range {@code [offset, offset + max)} are returned. These tests exercise that windowing behaviour together with the {@code remove()} contract and the constructor's argument validation.

@param the type of elements tested by this iterator.
The seven elements (indexes 0..6) wrapped by the iterators under test.
The {@link #testArray} exposed as a {@code List<E>}; rebuilt before each test.

Asserts that the iterator reports another element and that {@link Iterator#next()} returns the {@code expected} value. @param iter the iterator to advance @param expected the value the next element is expected to equal

Asserts that the iterator is exhausted: {@link Iterator#hasNext()} is {@code false} and {@link Iterator#next()} throws {@link NoSuchElementException}. @param iter the iterator expected to be exhausted
Test a decorated iterator bounded such that the first element returned is at an index greater its first element, and the last element returned is at an index less than its last element.
Window [offset=2, max=4) -> indexes 2,3,4,5 -> "c","d","e","f".
Test a decorated iterator bounded to a {@code max} of 0. The BoundedIterator should behave as if there are no more elements to return, since it is technically an empty iterator.
A max of 0 means no elements are in range, regardless of offset.

Test the case if the {@code max} passed to the constructor is greater than the size of the decorated iterator. The last element returned should be the same as the last element of the decorated iterator.
max=10 exceeds the 6 remaining elements, so iteration stops at the decorated iterator's end: indexes 1..6 -> "b".."g".
Test the case if a negative {@code max} is passed to the constructor. {@link IllegalArgumentException} is expected.
Test the case if a negative {@code offset} is passed to the constructor. {@link IllegalArgumentException} is expected.
Test the case if the {@code offset} passed to the constructor is greater than the decorated iterator's size. The BoundedIterator should behave as if there are no more elements to return.
offset=10 skips past every element, leaving nothing to return.
Test the {@code remove()} method being called twice without calling {@code next()} in between.
A second remove() with no intervening next() is illegal.
Test removing the first element. Verify that the element is removed from the underlying collection.
Removing the first in-range element does not affect the rest: "c".."f".
Test removing the last element. Verify that the element is removed from the underlying collection.
next() past the end throws an unmessaged NoSuchElementException.
remove() after the last next() still removes that last element ("f").
Test removing an element in the middle of the iterator. Verify that the element is removed from the underlying collection.
Iteration continues unaffected after a mid-stream remove: "e","f".
Test the case if the decorated iterator does not support the {@code remove()} method and throws an {@link UnsupportedOperationException}.
A decorated iterator whose remove() is unsupported.
BoundedIterator should propagate the decorated iterator's failure.
Test the {@code remove()} method being called without {@code next()} being called first.
remove() before any next() is illegal, even with a non-zero offset.
Test a decorated iterator bounded such that the {@code offset} is zero and the {@code max} is its size, in that the BoundedIterator should return all the same elements as its decorated iterator.
Window [offset=0, max=size) covers everything: "a".."g".
